## TaxoArena: per-domain LLM evaluation

[M.Sc. thesis, Technische Universität Berlin, August 2026 (Prof. Odej Kao's group). Grade 1.3. Then follow-up work on the same project.]{.page-meta}

::: {.lede}
**Question.** When does scoring language models per domain change which model you should use, or which comparison
you can trust, compared with one pooled leaderboard?
:::

### The thesis: a measurement of an LLM judge {.section-label}

The thesis ran an LLM-as-a-judge arena inside domain cells of MMLU-Pro, where the answer key is known, so the judge
itself could be measured.

- The judge's verdicts tracked answer correctness and the strength of the model, not the quality of the reasoning:
  agreement with the key was 91.1% when the correct model was also the stronger one of the pair, and 56.5% when it was
  the weaker.
- Across eight domains and eight models, it recovered the key's ordering on 196 of the 200 model pairs the key can
  separate.
- Rubrics written for each domain, compared with a generic prompt on the same comparisons, changed how often the
  judge abstained (13.0% vs 10.9%), not which model it ranked higher.
- A pre-registered negative result: finer domain cells did not carry different model rankings.

### Follow-up results {.section-label}

After the thesis, the same engine was extended to more benchmarks and larger model rosters.

- Routing each question to the best model for its domain beat the best single model by +2.67 points
  (95% CI [+1.46, +3.89], 5,907 items). Most of that gain comes from BBH: without BBH the interval includes zero,
  and on MMLU-Pro alone one model is best in every category, so there is nothing to route.
- On BBH, the gain held on a second roster of 342 Open LLM Leaderboard models, on a sealed side read once
  (+5.25 points, 95% CI [+2.95, +7.55]); a placebo that permutes the subtask labels produced no gain.
- On MATH, the choice of answer scorer alone reordered 18 models, with rank shifts of up to 15.
- Negative and open results are reported in the record, among them that the embedding taxonomy was not shown better
  than a simple per-source k-means baseline.

### Method {.section-label}

An evaluation engine in Kotlin with Python analysis tools, running up to 49 models on MMLU-Pro, BBH, SuperGPQA, MATH
and LiveCodeBench. The main tests are pre-registered, with explicit falsifiers and 95% intervals.
